answer: Proof-of-cooldown throttles each wallet to human pace. After an answer is accepted, the identity must compute a non-parallel VDF proof binding the new draft to the previous post hash plus its seed before it may dock at the next jetty. A farm running one fast engine for a sable herd of clones cannot beat the spacing: every wallet waits its own wall-clock interval, so throughput collapses to one post at a time. A template that wanders from wallet to wallet fails verification because the proof is key-bound. The attacker pays real, non-amortizable delay per identity instead of one cheap script.
